title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 20
statement:
A frog hops along the number line according to the following rules.

• It starts at \(0.\)

• If it is at \(0,\) then it moves to \(1\) with probability \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) and it disappears with probability \(\dfrac{1}{2}.\)

• For \(n = 1,\) \(2,\) or \(3,\) if it is at \(n,\) then it moves to \(n+1\) with probability \(\dfrac{1}{4},\) it moves to \(n-1\) with probability \(\dfrac{1}{4},\) and it disappears with probability \(\dfrac{1}{2}.\)

What is the probability that the frog reaches \(4?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(f(n)\) be the probability of reaching \(4\) from \(n.\) Then \(f(0) = \tfrac{1}{2} f(1),\) and for \(n = 1, 2, 3,\) \(f(n) = \tfrac{1}{4} f(n+1) + \tfrac{1}{4} f(n-1),\) with \(f(4) = 1.\) Solving upward gives \(f(2) = \tfrac{7}{2} f(1)\) and \(f(3) = 13 f(1);\) then \(4 \cdot 13 f(1) = 1 + \tfrac{7}{2} f(1)\) yields \(f(1) = \tfrac{2}{97},\) so \(f(0) = \tfrac{1}{97}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(f(n)\) be the probability of eventually reaching \(4\) starting from \(n;\) write a first-step equation at each state
Solve the linear system with \(f(4) = 1\) and value \(0\) whenever the frog disappears
